what_it_says: Released more carbon than they absorbed every year since 1990, mostly from wildfire and other disturbances
source: Domke et al. 2023, USDA Forest Service Resource Bulletin WO-101, Table 3

what_it_says: Fell about 17% from 1990 to 2023 (about 1,049 to 873 million metric tons CO2e a year, forest land remaining forest land)
source: EPA Inventory of U.S. Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Sinks 1990 to 2023, chapter 6

what_it_says: U.S. forests could become a net source of CO2 by 2070 under futures with high roundwood demand and net forest loss
source: USDA Forest Service 2023, 2020 RPA Assessment Key Findings, GTR WO-102 Chapter 1

what_it_says: Hold about 20% more aboveground carbon than unprotected forests; thinning releases some carbon in the short term
source: Faison et al. 2023, Forest Ecology and Management 544:121145

what_it_says: Mixing intensive production, lighter management and reserves could raise carbon sequestration 15% to 25% with no loss of harvest
source: Daigneault, Simons-Legaard and Weiskittel 2024, Forest Policy and Economics
